'''''VisionQuest''''' is an American television [[miniseries]] created by [[Terry Matalas]] for the streaming service [[Disney+]], based on [[Marvel Comics]] featuring the character [[Vision (Marvel Comics)|Vision]]. A [[Spinoff (media)|spin-off]] from the miniseries ''[[WandaVision]]'' (2021), it is [[List of Marvel Cinematic Universe television series (Marvel Studios)|the 18th television series]] in the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] (MCU) from [[Marvel Studios]] and is produced under its [[Marvel Television (Marvel Studios label)|Marvel Television]] label. The series shares continuity with [[List of Marvel Cinematic Universe films|the films of the MCU]]. It follows the synthezoid [[Vision (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Vision]] as he attempts to understand who he is by communicating with [[AI]] personas embedded in his programming, and goes on the run with a mysterious teenager who may be his reincarnated son. Matalas serves as [[showrunner]] and a director.

[[Paul Bettany]] reprises his role as Vision from previous MCU media, starring alongside [[James Spader]], [[Ruaridh Mollica]], [[Todd Stashwick]], [[Lauren Morais]], [[Orla Brady]], [[Diane Morgan]], [[Polly Frame]], [[Henry Lewis (playwright)|Henry Lewis]], [[Jonathan Sayer]], [[Emily Hampshire]], [[James D'Arcy]], [[Ben Crompton]], and [[T'Nia Miller]]. Development of a Vision series began by October 2022, with ''WandaVision''{{'s}} [[Jac Schaeffer]] as [[head writer]]. She was no longer involved by May 2024, when Matalas was redeveloping the series and Bettany was confirmed to be starring. It was described as the final installment in a trilogy that began with ''WandaVision'' and continued with ''[[Agatha All Along]]'' (2024). Filming began by March 2025 and [[Wrap (filmmaking)|wrapped]] in July, taking place at [[Pinewood Studios]] in London with Christopher J. Byrne, Gandja Monteiro, [[Vincenzo Natali]], and Matalas directing episodes. Casting for the AI personas included some returning MCU characters and actors.

''VisionQuest'' premiered on Disney+ on October 13, 2026, with its first two episodes, and will consist of eight episodes, concluding on November 10. It is part of [[Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase Six|Phase Six]] of the MCU.

== Premise ==
After being resurrected in ''[[WandaVision]]'' (2021), the [[synthezoid]] [[Vision (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Vision]] lives in hiding while he attempts to understand who he is by communicating with various [[AI]] personas that are embedded in his programming. When a bounty is placed on Vision's head, he goes on the run with a mysterious teenager who may be his reincarnated son.<ref name="D232026Marvel" />

== Cast and characters ==
<!-- Cast order per https://www.marvel.com/articles/tv-shows/visionquest-d23-2026-trailer-poster-paul-bettany -->
* [[Paul Bettany]] as [[Vision (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Vision]]:<br />A superpowered [[synthezoid]] and former [[Avengers (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Avenger]] created using the [[AI]]s J.A.R.V.I.S. and Ultron as well as the [[Mind Stone]]. Vision was killed in the film ''[[Avengers: Infinity War]]'' (2018) and then resurrected, with an all-white appearance and no memories or emotions, in the series ''[[WandaVision]]'' (2021).<ref name="MatalasRedevelop" /><ref name="BettanyMatalasOct2026DoG" /> After his memories were restored at the end of that series, Vision is now struggling to reconnect with those memories because he has no emotional attachment to them,<ref name="PremiereDate" /><ref name="BettanySep2026EW" /> with showrunner [[Terry Matalas]] calling him a "blank slate";<ref name="MatalasAug2026" /> he compared this journey to that of the ''[[Star Trek]]'' character [[Spock]] in the film ''[[Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home]]'' (1986).<ref name="MatalasSTLV2025Gizmodo" /> By the start of ''VisionQuest'', Vision has been posing as a human for years,<ref name="SetVisitCollider" /> and is now working at a pub under the name "Sherwood Ellis".<ref name="Eps1&2EasterEggs" /><ref name="Eps1&2RecapGizmodo" /> To cope with his [[identity crisis]], he retreats into his internal Mindspace, where various AI personas embedded in his programming manifest through human [[Avatar (computing)|avatar]]s.<ref name="Trailer2TIE" />
* [[James Spader]] as [[Ultron (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Ultron]]:<br />An AI created by [[Tony Stark (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Tony Stark]] and [[Bruce Banner (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Bruce Banner]] for a peacekeeping program, before developing a [[god complex]] and attempting to eradicate humanity. Since his android body was destroyed at the end of the film ''[[Avengers: Age of Ultron]]'' (2015),<ref name="Spader" /> Ultron has been uploaded by Vision into the Mindspace. There, he lives in a loft-like prison where he has access to the [[internet]] and spends his time painting,<ref name="SpaderAug2026SR" /><ref name="UltronAbsenceExplanation" /> which has given him a better perspective and understanding of humanity than Vision possesses;<ref name="MatalasUltronRetcon" /> Spader stated that Ultron is "probably the most human" of all the AIs in ''VisionQuest''.<ref name="BettanyOct2026Marvel" /> Matalas said the interactions between Vision and Ultron were a central dynamic for the series,<ref name="MatalasPHOct2025Dynamic" /> with Spader declaring that Ultron both loves and hates Vision,<ref name="UltronAbsenceExplanation" /> and that the two characters have a "sort of father-son-therapist-psychopath" relationship.<ref name="VisionKnowsWandaDead" /> Spader said ''VisionQuest'' allowed for further exploration of Ultron compared to his role in ''Age of Ultron'', calling him one of the series' "driving forces" alongside Vision and Tommy Maximoff.<ref name="SpaderUltronDrivingForces" />
* [[Ruaridh Mollica]] as [[Tommy Maximoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Tommy Maximoff]] and [[Thomas Shepherd (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Thomas Shepherd]]:<br />Tommy Maximoff is the [[Speedster (fiction)|speedster]] son of Vision and [[Wanda Maximoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Wanda Maximoff]]. In the series ''[[Agatha All Along]]'' (2024), his twin brother Billy Maximoff placed Tommy's soul into the body of Thomas Shepherd, a teenager who drowned.<ref name="NYCC2025EW" /><ref name="NYCC2025Variety" /><ref name="MollicaResume" /> In ''VisionQuest'', Tommy is an 18-year-old orphan who is newly out of the [[foster care system]] in London,<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|4}} and has been [[pickpocketing]] to survive, with Mollica stating that the character "likes to read and play people. There's a bit of [[Artful Dodger]]y."<ref name="SetVisitCollider" /> Tommy experiences visions stemming from his memories of Wanda's [[Hex (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Hex]] in ''WandaVision'', which leads him to face an identity crisis as he struggles to reconcile the personas of Tommy Maximoff and Thomas Shepherd.<ref name="MollicaColliderOct2026" /><ref name="MollicaVarietyOct2026" /> Mollica described Tommy as a grifter and small-time thief who is "lost in his life" and searching for a purpose,<ref name="MollicaSep2026BU" /> noting that the character has "had to build who he is by himself, and there's a loneliness to that, and a yearning for family".<ref name="MollicaVarietyOct2026" /> Mollica compared Tommy's journey of discovering his powers for the first time to that of [[Tobey Maguire]]'s [[Peter Parker (2002 film series character)|Peter Parker / Spider-Man]] in [[Sam Raimi]]'s film ''[[Spider-Man (2002 film)|Spider-Man]]'' (2002).<ref name="MollicaSpiderManComparison" /> Mollica drew inspiration from [[Matt Damon]]'s performance as Will Hunting in the film ''[[Good Will Hunting]]'' (1997) for Tommy's portrayal.<ref name="SetVisitCollider" />
* [[Todd Stashwick]] as [[Paladin (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Paladin]]:<br />A bounty hunter with a mysterious past who is hunting Vision.<ref name="MatalasSTLV2025Gizmodo" /><ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6}} Trained in all forms of martial arts and weaponry, he is the latest in a "centuries-long line" of bounty hunters who have held the title of "Paladin".<ref name="PaladinExplained" /> Matalas compared the character to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' bounty hunter [[Boba Fett]]. Stashwick described Paladin as a badass and said he was similar to previous roles that Matalas had written for him.<ref name="MatalasSTLV2025TM" /> Matalas drew inspiration from [[Tommy Lee Jones]]'s performance as Sam Gerard in the film ''[[The Fugitive (1993 film)|The Fugitive]]'' (1993) for Paladin's morally ambiguous personality.<ref name="SetVisitCollider" />
* [[Lauren Morais]] as [[Lisa Molinari (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Lisa Molinari]]:<br />A pickpocket and Tommy's partner-in-crime, with whom she develops romantic chemistry.<ref name="SetVisitCollider" /><ref name="MoraisMorgan" /> Mollica described Lisa as the only family Tommy has ever known,<ref name="MollicaSep2026SR" /> as the two characters met on a [[prisoner transport vehicle]].<ref name="SetVisitCollider" />
* [[Orla Brady]] as [[F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|F.R.I.D.A.Y.]]:<br />An AI created by Stark to replace J.A.R.V.I.S. as his personal assistant.<ref name="MatalasSTLV2025Gizmodo" /> In the Mindspace, F.R.I.D.A.Y. assists Vision with [[Social issue|socialization issues]], humor, and tactical ops.<ref name="New&ReturningCharacters" /> The series explores Stark's death in the film ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'' (2019) from F.R.I.D.A.Y.'s perspective, with Matalas noting that the character was unable to protect the one person she had been programmed to protect.<ref name="MatalasIronManDeath" />
* [[Diane Morgan]] as the Handler: An associate of Paladin who assists him in tracking down Vision<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6}}
* [[Polly Frame]] as Fiona Guthrie: The owner of the Old Selkie, a traditional Scottish pub in [[Edinburgh]] where Vision works<ref name="Eps1&2RecapGizmodo" />
* [[Henry Lewis (playwright)|Henry Lewis]] and [[Jonathan Sayer]] as [[D.U.M.-E.]] and [[U. (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|U.]], respectively:<br />A pair of robots created by Stark to assist him in his workshop.<ref name="LewisSayer" /> In the Mindspace, the human avatars of D.U.M.-E. and U. are presented as [[Handyman|handymen]], as both handle general maintenance, with D.U.M.-E. also being responsible for [[Fire suppression system|fire suppression]], while U.—who is [[Muteness|mute]]—acts as a [[defragger]] and [[videographer]].<ref name="AICharacterGuide" /> Sayer stated that D.U.M.-E. and U. function like [[twin]]s who are "super in sync", and added that both characters want to show the other AIs in the Mindspace that they are "equal and able to mix in with them".<ref name="SetVisitCollider" />
* [[Emily Hampshire]] as [[E.D.I.T.H.]]:<br />An AI created by Stark that runs an [[augmented reality]] security and defense system. After Stark's death, control of E.D.I.T.H. was briefly bequeathed to [[Peter Parker (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Peter Parker / Spider-Man]] in the film ''[[Spider-Man: Far From Home]]'' (2019).<ref name="Hampshire" /> Since then, E.D.I.T.H. has been "reprogrammed for fun",<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|5}} shifting to handle recreation, [[game theory]], and weaponry in the Mindspace.<ref name="New&ReturningCharacters" /> Hampshire described the character as "basically the embodiment of all the human thrill-seeking joy in life", as well as "part [[cheerleader]], part AI, part malfunctioning [[theme park]] ride".<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|5}}
* [[James D'Arcy]] as [[J.A.R.V.I.S.]]:<br />The first AI created by Stark, developed to serve as his personal assistant before being used to create Vision in ''Age of Ultron''.<ref name="NYCC2025" /> In the Mindspace, J.A.R.V.I.S.'s human avatar is a [[butler]]-like figure resembling [[Edwin Jarvis (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Edwin Jarvis]], who served as the inspiration for his creation,<ref name="D232026Empire" /><ref name="AICharacterGuide" /> and he works on security, [[housekeeping]], and [[encryption]].<ref name="New&ReturningCharacters" />
* [[Ben Crompton]] as Clancy: A guard on a prison bus that attempted to transport Tommy and Lisa to Saint Mabyn's Psychiatric Sanitarium.{{citation needed|date=October 2026}}
* [[T'Nia Miller]] as [[Jocasta (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Jocasta]]: A cunning and powerful android driven by revenge.<ref name="Miller" /><ref name="MatalasSep2026TVI" /> Miller described the character as a badass.<ref name="MillerSep2026Diva" />

Additionally, actors reprising their MCU roles include [[Joe Locke]] as [[Billy Maximoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Billy Maximoff]], Wanda and Vision's sorcerer son and Tommy's younger twin brother whose soul inhabited [[William Kaplan (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|William Kaplan]]'s body after his death in ''Agatha All Along'';<ref name="Locke" /> and [[Faran Tahir]] as [[Raza (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Raza]], the leader of the [[Ten Rings (organization)|Ten Rings]] faction that kidnapped Stark in the film ''[[Iron Man (2008 film)|Iron Man]]'' (2008). Raza was seemingly killed by [[Obadiah Stane (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Obadiah Stane]] in that film.<ref name="Tahir" /> Also appearing are Cristian Lavin as a mercenary,<ref name="Lavin" /> and [[Mary McDonnell]] in an undisclosed role.<ref name="McDonnell" /> The character [[Human Torch (android)|Jim Hammond / Human Torch]], an android capable of controlling fire, will appear in the series.<ref name="HumanTorchRetcon" />

== Production ==
=== Background ===
In March 2009, [[Marvel Studios]] hired writers to help come up with creative ways to launch its lesser-known properties, including the [[Marvel Comics]] character [[Vision (Marvel Comics)|Vision]].<ref name="Writers2009" /> [[Paul Bettany]] was cast as the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] (MCU) incarnation of [[Vision (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Vision]] for the film ''[[Avengers: Age of Ultron]]'' (2015). This version of the character is an [[synthezoid]] who is partially created from [[J.A.R.V.I.S.]], an [[AI]] assistant voiced by Bettany in earlier [[MCU films]]. Following Vision's death in the film ''[[Avengers: Infinity War]]'' (2018), Bettany was revealed to be portraying a reassembled and reactivated version of the character in the [[Disney+]] series ''[[WandaVision]]'' (2021). This version was referred to as "White Vision" or simply "The Vision",<ref name="BettanyWhiteVision" /><ref name="SchaefferETMar2021" /><ref name="TheVisionBettany" /> and has an all-white appearance, similar to when the comic book character was resurrected with an all-white body and no memories or emotions.<ref name="BettanyWhiteVision" />

[[Jac Schaeffer]], the [[head writer]] of ''WandaVision'', signed a three-year overall television deal with Marvel Studios in May 2021 to develop additional Disney+ projects.<ref name="SchaefferDeal" /> By October 2022, they were developing a series called ''Vision Quest'',<ref name="SneiderVisionQuest" /><ref name="DeadlineVisionQuest" /> which would center on Bettany's "White Vision". Schaeffer was set as head writer after working on another ''WandaVision'' spin-off series, ''[[Agatha All Along]]'' (2024).<ref name="DeadlineVisionQuest" /> Development of a Vision series was rumored as early as March 2021<!-- The THR article says "two years ago" from Oct 2022, for the Giant Freakin Robot article, given the URL at that time listed the publish date as "2 years ago". However, the article discusses the content of WandaVision, and the earliest web archive of the article puts the publication date as March 23, 2021. That archive is here: https://web.archive.org/web/20210323160914/https://www.giantfreakinrobot.com/ent/exclusive-vision-series.html -->.<ref name="THRVisionQuest" /> The name "Vision Quest" was previously used for a comic book storyline in ''[[West Coast Avengers]]'' vol. 2 #42–45 (1988–1989);<ref name="SneiderVisionQuest" /><ref name="VarietyVisionQuest" /> it was unclear if the series would be a direct adaptation of that comic.<ref name="SneiderVisionQuest" /> A [[writers' room]] was set to be formed in early November 2022,<ref name="SneiderVisionQuest" /><ref name="DeadlineVisionQuest" /> to include Peter Cameron, [[Megan McDonnell]], and Eileen Shim.<ref name="CameronMcDonnell" /><ref name="Shim" /> Cameron and McDonnell worked on ''WandaVision'' and ''Agatha All Along''.<ref name="CameronMcDonnell" /> ''Vision Quest'' was expected to follow "White Vision" as he attempts to regain his memories and humanity, with potential for [[Elizabeth Olsen]] to reprise her MCU role as Vision's wife [[Wanda Maximoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Wanda Maximoff / Scarlet Witch]].<ref name="DeadlineVisionQuest" />

=== Development ===
[[File:Terry Matalas Photo Op GalaxyCon Austin 2023.jpg|thumb|upright|Showrunner [[Terry Matalas]] was hired by May 2024 to redevelop the series.]]
By October 2023, Marvel Studios shifted its creative philosophy to a more traditional television development process, moving away from head writers and beginning to hire dedicated [[showrunner]]s for its series.<ref name="MarvelStudiosTVOverhaul" /> By May 2024, Schaeffer was no longer developing ''Vision Quest'' due to her focus on making ''Agatha All Along'',<ref name="MatalasRedevelop" /> as well as for "personal reasons" according to Bettany,<ref name="BettanySep2026EW" /> with [[Terry Matalas]] joining to redevelop the series and serve as its showrunner.<ref name="MatalasRedevelop" /> Marvel Studios hired Matalas after being impressed with his work on the [[Star Trek: Picard season 3|third season]] of ''[[Star Trek: Picard]]'' (2023), with Marvel Studios president [[Kevin Feige]] being a particular fan of the ''[[Star Trek]]'' franchise.<ref name="MatalasRedevelop" /><ref name="FeigeMatalasFan" /> Matalas was also set to direct for the series, alongside Christopher J. Byrne, [[Vincenzo Natali]], and ''Agatha All Along'' episodic director Gandja Monteiro.<ref name="Directors" />

Matalas met with Schaeffer upon joining the project, and Marvel Studios executive [[Brad Winderbaum]] said it would be a "love letter" to the work Schaeffer had done, while being unique to Matalas.<ref name="WinderbaumEWSchafferMatalas" /> The series was still being referred to by Marvel as ''Vision Quest'',<ref name="Livanos" /><ref name="WinderbaumSep2024Name" /><ref name="Tahir" /> but ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' said this was not its official title.<ref name="Spader" /><ref name="Stashwick" /> Disney was referring to the series as simply ''Vision'' by May 2025,<ref name="DisneyUpfronts2025BGR" /> before the title was officially announced as ''VisionQuest'' that October. The series has been described as the final installment of the trilogy that began with ''WandaVision'' and continued with ''Agatha All Along''.<ref name="NYCC2025" /> Describing the relationship to those other two series, Matalas said ''VisionQuest'' was more of a sequel to ''WandaVision'', while touching on some elements from ''Agatha All Along''.<ref name="MatalasSep2026Polygon" /> Marvel Studios's [[Mary Livanos]], who worked on those two series, returned as an executive producer for ''VisionQuest'',<ref name="Livanos" /> alongside Bettany, Schaeffer, and Byrne,<ref name="ProjectProfile" /> while Roopesh Parekh was a producer.<ref name="FilmingWrap" /> The series is being released under Marvel Studios' "[[Marvel Television (Marvel Studios label)|Marvel Television]]" label.<ref name="MatalasRedevelop" />

=== Writing ===
A writers' room opened during the week of May 20, 2024,<ref name="MatalasTHR" /> featuring Cindy Appel, [[Michael Taylor (screenwriter)|Michael Taylor]], Christopher Monfette, Nicole Falsetti, and Matthew Okumura, alongside Matalas.<ref name="WGACredits" /> Matalas described ''VisionQuest'' as an adventure and mystery drama, while also having elements of surreal comedy. The basis of the series was inspired by two scenes: the final conversation between Vision and his creator, the villainous AI [[Ultron (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Ultron]], in ''Age of Ultron''; and the "[[Ship of Theseus]]" discussion between the two versions of Vision in ''WandaVision''.<ref name="MatalasSep2026Polygon" /> Matalas stated that the former scene was the "launching point" for ''VisionQuest'', while Bettany described the series as a "mash-up of the ''[[The Adventures of Pinocchio|Pinocchio]]'' and ''[[Frankenstein]]'' stories".<ref name="BettanyMatalasOct2026DoG" />

''VisionQuest'' is set around 2028, 18 months after ''Agatha All Along'' and years after the events of ''WandaVision'',<ref name="Timeline" /><ref name="Timeline2" /> at the end of which Vision's memories were restored.<ref name="PremiereDate" /> It focuses on the character's struggle to reconnect with those memories because he has no emotional attachment to them,<ref name="NYCC2025EW" /><ref name="BettanySep2026EW" /> causing him to undergo an [[identity crisis]].<ref name="BettanyAug2026Empire" /><ref name="MatalasSep2026TVI" /> As part of his attempts to understand who he is, Vision interacts with the human population disguised as one of them during the day, while at night he retreats into the [[quantum processor]]s of his own mind, where he has created the Mindspace—a gigantic mansion filled with environments he can alter at will. There, he communicates with various AI personas he rescued from the [[Avengers Compound (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Avengers Compound]] and which are embedded in his programming;<ref name="BettanySep2026EW" /><ref name="MatalasUltronRetcon" /> Vision encourages all these AIs to adopt human [[Avatar (computing)|avatar]]s as he does,<ref name="UltronHumanForm" /><ref name="USAHeraldSep2026" /> and they possess distinct characteristics that help him understand different human qualities and abilities.<ref name="BettanyAug2026Empire" /><ref name="BettanySep2026EW" /> Bettany said the AI personas are inside the Mindspace because Vision had "been saving and copying and pasting them to keep them alive", including Ultron, whom Bettany stated "has to be kept behind a pretty impressive [[Firewall (computing)|firewall]] because he's a psychopath".<ref name="BettanyColliderAIsInHead" /> Ultron returns in ''VisionQuest'' following his apparent death in ''Age of Ultron'' because the creative team wanted to include a character who was "really strong for Vision to play off of", and since they did not have access to Wanda, Ultron was chosen instead.<ref name="VisionKnowsWandaDead" /> Bettany said that the series' story revolves largely around the relationship between Vision and Ultron.<ref name="EverythingKnowTF" /> Despite Wanda not appearing in the series,<ref name="MatalasMoreSeasons" /> Matalas confirmed that Vision is aware of her death in the MCU film ''[[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness]]'' (2022).<ref name="VisionKnowsWandaDead" />

The series continues the ''WandaVision'' trilogy theme of exploring parenthood, specifically fatherhood. Winderbaum said ''VisionQuest'' was about three generations—a grandfather, father, and son—and would explore if a man who had an abusive father could be a good father himself.<ref name="WinderbaumMarvelPodcastJan2026" /> Bettany said ''VisionQuest'' explores [[intergenerational trauma]] with fathers and sons, similar to how ''WandaVision'' explores grief, as well as "denial of pain, and denial of your own truth, and coming to terms with who and what you are".<ref name="BettanyThemes" /> Matalas said each episode feels like a different kind of film, similar to how each episode of ''WandaVision'' pays homage to a different era of American [[sitcoms]].<ref name="MatalasPHOct2025DiffFilms" /> Winderbaum said Matalas "knows the lore" of the MCU and the series would be rewarding for fans who had followed the franchise for years.<ref name="NYCC2025EW" /> Matalas described one scene in the finale as "a Marvel dream".<ref name="MatalasPHOct2025Dynamic" />

=== Casting ===
{{Multiple image
| total_width       = 300
| image1            = Paul Bettany - Los Angeles Comic Con 2025.jpg
| image2            = James Spader by Gage Skidmore.jpg
| footer            = [[Paul Bettany]] and [[James Spader]] reprise their MCU roles as [[Vision (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Vision]] and [[Ultron (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Ultron]], respectively.
| align             = left
}}
Bettany was confirmed to be reprising his MCU role of Vision with the news of the series' redevelopment in May 2024.<ref name="MatalasRedevelop" /> In August, [[James Spader]] was set to reprise his role as Ultron from ''Age of Ultron''.<ref name="Spader" /> The character also appears as a human in the series because Matalas did not want him to look like a "[[Computer-generated imagery|CGI]] robot 24/7" incapable of expressing emotions or doing the things Spader can do with "just the twitch of an eyebrow".<ref name="UltronHumanForm" /> [[Todd Stashwick]], who worked with Matalas on the television series ''[[12 Monkeys (TV series)|12 Monkeys]]'' (2015–2018) and ''Picard'', joined the cast a month later.<ref name="Stashwick" /> In January 2025, [[Faran Tahir]] was revealed to be reprising his role as [[Raza (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Raza]] from the first MCU film, ''[[Iron Man (2008 film)|Iron Man]]'' (2008).<ref name="Tahir" /> [[Ruaridh Mollica]] joined the cast a month later as a character referred to as "Tucker",<ref name="Mollica" /> and [[T'Nia Miller]] was cast in the leading role of the android [[Jocasta (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Jocasta]] in May.<ref name="Miller" /> Soon after, [[Emily Hampshire]] was revealed to be portraying the key role of [[E.D.I.T.H.]],<ref name="Hampshire" /> an AI introduced in the MCU film ''[[Spider-Man: Far From Home]]'' (2019) where she was voiced by assistant editor Dawn Michelle King.<ref name="AIActorsCB" /> Matalas wrote the role with Hampshire in mind, as they had previously worked together on ''12 Monkeys''.<ref name="SetVisitCollider" />

Matalas revealed in August 2025 that Stashwick was playing the comic character [[Paladin (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Paladin]], and that ''Picard'' star [[Orla Brady]] was portraying the AI [[F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|F.R.I.D.A.Y.]], replacing [[Kerry Condon]] who voiced the character in several MCU projects.<ref name="MatalasSTLV2025Gizmodo" /> [[Mary McDonnell]] was revealed as part of the cast the next month.<ref name="McDonnell" /> In October, several more cast members were revealed: [[Henry Lewis (playwright)|Henry Lewis]] and [[Jonathan Sayer]] as [[D.U.M.-E.]] and [[U. (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|U.]], respectively, two robots seen in the MCU films;<ref name="LewisSayer" /> and [[James D'Arcy]] as J.A.R.V.I.S., the AI originally voiced by Bettany in the MCU films. D'Arcy portrayed [[Edwin Jarvis (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Edwin Jarvis]], the human inspiration for the AI J.A.R.V.I.S., in several MCU projects.<ref name="NYCC2025" /><ref name="AIActorsCB" /> Matalas hired Lewis and Sayer after seeing them perform in the play ''[[Peter Pan Goes Wrong]]''.<ref name="SetVisitCollider" /><ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6}} That same month, Mollica was revealed to be portraying [[Tommy Maximoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Tommy Maximoff]] and [[Thomas Shepherd (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Thomas Shepherd]], taking over from [[Jett Klyne]] who portrayed Tommy in ''WandaVision'' and the MCU film ''[[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness]]'' (2022).<ref name="NYCC2025EW" /><ref name="NYCC2025" /> Mollica previously auditioned for the MCU role of [[Billy Maximoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Billy Maximoff]], Tommy's twin brother.<ref name="MollicaBillyRole" /> In November, [[Lauren Morais]] and [[Diane Morgan]] were respectively revealed to be portraying [[Lisa Molinari (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Lisa Molinari]] and the Handler, the latter an associate of Paladin.<ref name="MoraisMorgan" /><ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6}} In October 2026, Mollica announced that [[Joe Locke]] would reprise his MCU role of Billy Maximoff from ''Agatha All Along'' in the series.<ref name="Locke" /> Additional castings include Cristian Lavin as a mercenary,<ref name="Lavin" /> and [[Polly Frame]] as Fiona Guthrie.<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6}}

=== Design ===
Will Hughes-Jones served as the production designer for ''VisionQuest'',<ref name="Jones" /><ref name="SetVisitSR" /> with Sarah Young as the costume designer after she was an assistant costume designer on ''Age of Ultron''.<ref name="Young" /><ref name="SetVisitCollider" /> Hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Frances "Fran" Hounsom also worked on the series.<ref name="USAHeraldSep2026" /> Despite ''VisionQuest'' not using [[generative AI]], Hughes-Jones deliberately emulated the flawed aesthetic of AI software renderings in the design of the Mindspace—including stair banisters that lead nowhere, chairs built into walls, and wonky furniture.<ref name="NoGenAI" /> Over 40 custom "Vision"-branded props were created for the Mindspace kitchen, including Vision's Mustard, Firewall Hot Sauce, Mindstone Soup,<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|7}} InfiniDairy, and Vibranium Foil.<ref name="Eps1&2EasterEggs" /> Matalas stated that the environments in the Mindspace resemble [[screensaver]]s with "vibrant, bright, almost ''[[Mario Bros.]]''-like colors".<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|7}}

Young's team had to recreate the White Vision suit for ''VisionQuest'' because only two original examples from ''WandaVision'' remained, and they had deteriorated during storage.<ref name="USAHeraldSep2026" /> Vision's [[Pinstripes|pinstriped suit]] features a robotic code incorporated into the garment's stitching, which was written by Matalas alongside Young. Similarly, Vision's costume reflects the silhouette of his robotic form, including a jumper with the [[Mind Stone (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Mind Stone]] in its center. Tommy's costumes were designed based on the color palette of his counterpart from the comics, [[Speed (character)|Speed]].<ref name="SetVisitSR" /> E.D.I.T.H. possessed an extensive wardrobe consisting of 21 distinct outfits—more than any other character in the series—including those of a boxer, bullfighter, priest, race car driver, and field medic; a consistent color palette of red, blue, and yellow was developed to maintain continuity despite the frequent costume changes. Costume references for E.D.I.T.H. included [[Amelia Earhart]], female [[World War II]] pilots, [[Formula One]] branding, and [[Antique aircraft|vintage aviation]], all reinterpreted through the Mindspace aesthetic.<ref name="USAHeraldSep2026" /><ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|8}} Paladin's clothing is deliberately less conspicuous than in the comics, allowing the character to blend into the crowd. His wardrobe includes both tactical and street versions of his jacket.<ref name="USAHeraldSep2026" />

=== Filming ===
[[File:Hatfield House.jpg|thumb|right|alt=Exterior shot of Hatfield House in January 2002|Location filming took place around the United Kingdom, including at Hatfield House.]]
[[Principal photography]] began by March 14, 2025, at [[Pinewood Studios]] in London,<ref name="FilmingStart" /> under the [[working title]] ''Tin Man'',<ref name="WorkingTitle" /> with Byrne, Monteiro, Natali, and Matalas directing.<ref name="Directors" /> [[Christopher Ross (cinematographer)|Christopher Ross]], Neville Kidd, and [[Ben Smithard]] were the cinematographers.<ref name="Ross" /><ref name="KiddSmithard" /><ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|1}} [[Location shooting]] took place in and around London,<ref name="Jones" />{{Independent source inline|date=June 2026}} as well as at various sites across the United Kingdom, including [[Hatfield House]], which served as the setting for Horton Manor, and [[White Waltham Airfield]], used for scenes set in Paladin's jet hangar.<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6–7}} Two practical sets were extensively used in the production of ''VisionQuest'': the first was a build spanning two streets, representing the crime-ridden city of [[Madripoor (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Madripoor]], which included the [[Princess Bar]]; and the second was the Mindspace mansion.<ref name="SetVisitSR" /> The latter set took 14 weeks to build, and featured seven fully functional rooms—including a kitchen, living room, dining room, entrance hall, corridor, [[Boiler room (business)|boiler room]], and cinema—each designed to connect physically, allowing for continuous camera movement.<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|6–8}} Filming [[Wrap (filmmaking)|wrapped]] in late July 2025,<ref name="FilmingWrap" /> and was completed in August,<ref name="Jones" />{{third-party inline|date=November 2025}} when Matalas indicated that production spanned seven months.<ref name="MatalasSTLV2025TM" />

=== Post-production ===
Drew Nichols, Amelia Allwarden, Jamie Gross, Christopher Gay, and McKenna Cook served as editors for the series.<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|1}} John Haley served as visual effects supervisor, while Jonathan Barrass was the special effects supervisor. There were over 280 practical effects in the series, including magnetic rigging for Vision's flight scenes and interactive [[LED]] reflections for the Mindspace walls.<ref name="FinalProductionNotes" />{{rp|8}}

=== Music ===
[[Mick Giacchino]], the son of frequent MCU composer [[Michael Giacchino]], was revealed to be composing the series' score in March 2026.<ref name="Giacchino" />

== Marketing ==
Footage from the series was included in a [[sizzle reel]] that was shown at Disney's [[Upfront (advertising)|upfront]] presentation in May 2025.<ref name="DisneyUpfronts2025BGR" /> Bettany and Winderbaum promoted the series during a [[Marvel Studios Animation|Marvel Animation]] and Marvel Television panel at [[New York Comic Con]] 2025, where footage was shown.<ref name="NYCC2025" /> Mekishana Pierre and Nick Romano at ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' noted the "trippy setting" of a mansion in Vision's mind where he sees personifications of other AIs from the MCU, comparing this to the "reality-warping vibes" of ''WandaVision'' and ''Agatha All Along''.<ref name="NYCC2025EW" /> The appearance of Spader as Ultron in both robot and human forms was also noted by commentators.<ref name="NYCC2025EW" /><ref name="NYCC2025Variety" /><ref name="NYCC2025IGN" /> Bettany and Matalas promoted the series during the [[53rd Saturn Awards]] ceremony in March 2026,<ref name="BettanyMatalasSCMarch2026" /> and Bettany appeared at Disney's May upfront presentation to announce the premiere date and show more footage.<ref name="PremiereDate" />

At Disney's [[D23 (Disney)#2026|D23]] convention in August 2026, a ''VisionQuest'' booth displayed a screen framed like a painting which showed a mysterious figure engulfed in flames. The image would [[glitch]] to show glimpses of Ultron. Commentators believed the fiery figure could be the character [[Human Torch (android)|Jim Hammond / Human Torch]], an android whose body was used to create Vision in the comics.<ref name="D232026BoothCommentary" /> Also at the convention, Feige, Bettany, and Spader promoted the series during a panel and debuted the first trailer before it was released online.<ref name="D232026Marvel" /> The trailer, which featured the song "[[Losing My Mind]]",<ref name="LosingMyMind" /> was described as "trippy" by Kirsten Chuba and Aaron Couch at ''The Hollywood Reporter'',<ref name="D232026THR" /> "mind-bending" by James Hibbs for ''[[Radio Times]]'',<ref name="D232026RT" /> and "as weird, if not weirder, than ''WandaVision''" by Michael McWhertor of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]''.<ref name="D232026Polygon" />

A second trailer was released on October 1, 2026. Michael Walsh of ''[[Nerdist]]'' praised the trailer, calling it an "absolute banger" that presented ''VisionQuest'' as "surreal, mysterious, heartfelt, and funny", while also bringing "real stakes" for both the series' characters and the MCU as a whole.<ref name="Trailer2Nerdist" /> Bettany promoted the series at [[San Diego Comic-Con]] Málaga 2026 on October 3, where the first 22 minutes of the premiere episode were screened.<ref name="SDCCMalaga2026" /> Bettany further promoted ''VisionQuest'' alongside Spader, Mollica, Hampshire, and Matalas at New York Comic Con 2026 that same month, where the series' first episode was screened.<ref name="NYCC2026Marvel" /> Also part of that convention was an immersive [[pop-up exhibition]] titled "Controlled, Altered, Deleted: The ''VisionQuest'' Collection", which was on display at Studio 525 in New York on October 9 and 10. The exhibition featured parodies of famous paintings, such as [[Grant Wood]]'s ''[[American Gothic]]'' (1930) and [[Edward Hopper]]'s ''[[Nighthawks (painting)|Nighthawks]]'' (1942), among others.<ref name="ArtGallery" /> An episode of ''VisionQuest'' will be screened at the [[Savannah College of Art and Design|SCAD]] [[Savannah Film Festival]]'s third annual TV Sidebar on October 26—an event where Bettany will receive the Virtuoso Award.<ref name="SCADFilmFestival" />

== Release ==
''VisionQuest'' had its first two episodes screened at the 2026 [[BFI London Film Festival]] on October 12,<ref name="LondonFilmFestivalEmpire" /><ref name="LondonFilmFestivalSR" /> ahead of their premiere on Disney+ on October 13;<ref name="ReleaseSchedule" /> the series was originally scheduled to premiere on October 14.<ref name="PremiereDate" /> The remaining six episodes will be released weekly in two-episode blocks, followed by the final two episodes releasing individually on November 3 and 10, respectively.<ref name="ReleaseSchedule" /> It is a part of [[Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase Six|Phase Six]] of the MCU.<ref name="MoraisMorgan" />

== Reception ==
On review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]], 90% of 55 critics gave the season a positive review, and the average of rated reviews was 7.3 out of 10. The critics' consensus reads, "Picking up where ''WandaVision'' left off, this series investigates the humanity beneath the robot, where the artificial becomes reality with heart, deliberate emotion, and a clear-eyed ''VisionQuest''."<ref name="RottenTomatoes">{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes |id=visionquest |type=tv |title=VisionQuest |access-date=October 14, 2026}}{{cbignore}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 64 out of 100 based on 25 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{Cite Metacritic |id=visionquest |type=tv |title=VisionQuest |access-date=October 13, 2026}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

== Future ==
In September 2026, Matalas said he had ideas for how the story of ''VisionQuest'' could continue in future seasons,<ref name="MatalasMoreSeasons" /> while Bettany said the series was introducing a "new type" of Vision and would be a "springboard" for the character's future MCU appearances.<ref name="BettanySep2026EW" />
